description: vornik-companion for Codex: recall-nudge.sh, an OFFLINE just-in-time nudge. PreToolUse(Bash) parses the shell command text (it never runs it) for paths a read program (cat, sed, rg, grep, find, ls, ...) was pointed at; on the 3rd read into one subsystem with no recent successful recall it tells the model to recall that subsystem's design. PostToolUse(mcp__vornik__recall) records that a recall returned. It fires once per subsystem per session, never blocks, makes no network call and keeps no content (LLD 23, Recall nudge for Codex, 2026-10-13). Codex runs it only after you trust it; set VORNIK_NUDGE=off to silence it. hints.sh, the same script as the Claude Code bundle's (kept byte-equal by a test), shows the companion's just-in-time hints: SessionStart runs its network turn detached (fetch the catalogue, upload earlier sessions' outcomes), and PostToolUse on every tool and UserPromptSubmit detect a commit, a design edit (from apply_patch's headers) and a failed test run (from its output; Codex gives a hook no exit status). Each hint fires at most once per session; the hooks keep hint ids and counters only. Set VORNIK_HINTS=off to silence them (LLD 2026-08-20 companion hardening §13.12, GitHub #634).
